paper_title: Are Large Language Models Really Good Logical Reasoners A Comprehensive   Evaluation and Beyond
caption: Visualization on the metric of answer correctness.
model_annotation: This 3D bar chart visualizes the accuracy (answer correctness) of three large language models—Davinci-003, ChatGPT, and BARD—across three reasoning types: Inductive, Abductive, and Deductive, as well as a combined "Mix" category. The vertical axis represents accuracy, scaled from 0 to 0.8 with tick marks at 0.2 intervals, indicating a linear scale. The horizontal axis lists the three models in the order: Davinci-003, ChatGPT, BARD. The depth axis (front-to-back) displays the reasoning types: Inductive, Abductive, Deductive, and Mix, arranged from left to right in that order. Each model has four bars corresponding to the four reasoning types, with colors ranging from blue (lower accuracy) to yellow (higher accuracy), suggesting a gradient-based color scheme that reflects performance. For Davinci-003, the accuracy ranges from approximately 0.3 (Inductive) to 0.7 (Mix). For ChatGPT, accuracy ranges from about 0.2 (Inductive) to 0.7 (Mix). For BARD, accuracy ranges from roughly 0.4 (Inductive) to 0.8 (Mix). The bars are grouped by model along the horizontal axis and stacked by reasoning type along the depth axis, forming a 3x4 grid of bars. The tallest bars (highest accuracy) are consistently observed in the "Mix" category for all three models, while the shortest bars (lowest accuracy) appear in the "Inductive" category for ChatGPT and Davinci-003. The chart uses a 3D perspective with grid lines for depth and height, and no explicit legend is provided, but the color gradient visually encodes the accuracy level.
